transcript: Pablo Picasso was born in 1881 in Malaga, Spain. He is one of the most influential painters of the 20th century, leaving behind tens of thousands of works in his lifetime, including sculpture, prints, and ceramics. In his 20s Picasso moved to Paris and for a time produced dark toned paintings of what is called his blue period. After his rose period, his style would change dramatically again and again. In 1907 Picasso unveiled Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. The work shocked the art world with its bold method of breaking the human figure Into geometric shapes It became the starting point of a new art movement That would later be called Cubism Cubism overturned from its very ground The long western tradition of painting an object From a single perspective Picasso and breakthrough shapes Seen from many angles at once on a single canvas In 1937, in the middle of the Spanish Civil War The Nazi German Air Force bombed the small town of Gernica Angered by the suffering, Picasso completed the enormous painting Gernica in only a few weeks It became a symbol that called the cruelty of war To the attention of the world Picasso never settled into a single style It took me a long time to learn to pay like a child He sat in his later years Perhaps no one expanded the horizon Of contemporary art As widely as he did
